instructions: Speak like a thoughtful documentary narrator inside a product film. Warm, precise, unhurried. Conversational American English. Slight breath after numbers. Never salesy, never chirpy, never robotic. Pronounce Unilog as YOO-nih-log. Pronounce thExplorers as the Explorers. Pronounce SKU as skew. Pronounce MPN as M-P-N.

lines.text: A distributor sends you six columns. A part number. A short description. A few brand placeholders. That is the entire input. Unilog turns it into a two-hundred-fifty-two column delivery record — and every filled cell cites the page it came from.

The pipeline is deterministic. Resolve the manufacturer. Classify to a leaf. Extract from official HTML, JSON-L-D, and PDFs. Normalize, validate, compose five descriptions. Rules first. A language model is last-mile only. No evidence — the field stays blank.
This is the live product. One take. No mocked data.
Paste a Frigidaire dishwasher part number. Enrich. The record comes back with invoice, mobile, and short descriptions — inside their character limits — plus attributes, each with a source URL.
Open any row. The evidence drawer shows exactly where a value came from. Two hundred thirteen columns are blank on purpose. No manufacturer evidence — so nothing was invented.
Now the sample catalog. One thousand rows, streamed live. Every SKU classified. About thirty-nine fields filled per row — only what the sources actually support.
Confidence stays honest. High requires an external manufacturer page. Everything else is flagged for review.
Against the organizer expected output: one hundred percent. Sixty-three of sixty-three on Frigidaire. Seventy-one of seventy-one on Whirlpool.
Export is the delivery format they asked for. CSV. Excel. And a provenance file for every cell.

That is the trust bar. One hundred thirty-four fields matched. One thousand of one thousand rows classified. Seventy-seven hermetic tests. Two seconds. No network. High confidence is never self-cited. Blank beats invented.
Unilog. Evidence-first product intelligence for industrial commerce. Built by the Explorers for UniHack twenty twenty-six. The prototype is live. The repository is public.
